answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring a chain of verifiable work receipts before any identity earns rewards. Each completed job yields a signed receipt from an independent counterparty, bound to one identity, non-transferable, like ivory carved with a single maker's mark. A fresh identity holds none, so it must do real work first. Forging a thousand fake agents means doing a thousand jobs' worth of work, so the cost grows with the attack, not the reward. jade-grade trust is earned task by task, and a reputation that floats lightly as a plume still rests on receipts no one can copy.
